newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ISLES SIGN NEMCHINOV, RE-SIGN LAPOINTE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ISLES SIGN NEMCHINOV, RE-SIGN LAPOINTE.

text.p: The New York Islanders continued their free-agent signing blitz Wednesday by agreeing to terms with centre Sergei Nemchinov, who finished the 1996-97 season with the Vancouver Canucks.
The Islanders, who have vowed to spend some of new owner John Spano's money to attract big-name free agents, also re-signed centre Claude Lapointe.

General manager Mike Milbury has said he would continue to seek free agents despite the status of Spano, who has made no payments to former owner John Pickett since the sale of the franchise was approved by the National Hockey League's Board of Governors more than four months ago.
Spano has agreed not to be involved in the operation of the Islanders and is not authorised to take any actions on behalf of the team, league officials announced Monday.

The 33-year-old, Moscow-born Nemchinov returns to New York, where he spent six-plus seasons with the rival Rangers. He started last season with the Rangers, but was traded to Vancouver on March 8 as part of a four-player deal.
Nemchinov was bothered by a back injury and played only six games for the Canucks. He combined for eight goals and 16 assists in 69 games.
Nemchinov, a checking specialist, helped the Rangers end a 54-year-old Stanley Cup drought in 1994, becoming one of the first four Russians to have their names etched on the Cup.

Like Nemchinov, the 28-year-old Lapointe also is a solid defensive forward. Lapointe signed with the Islanders as a free agent prior to last season and was fifth on the team with a surprising 13 goals. He finished strongly, collecting nine goals and three assists in the final 26 games.
